questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.107, an arm signal to stop or suddenly decrease speed is given by extending the hand and arm downward from the vehicle's left side.

questions.prompt: When is it appropriate and legal for a driver to activate four-way emergency flashing hazard lights in Texas?

options.text: Whenever driving through routine afternoon rain showers to increase notice
When cruising at sixty miles per hour on an interstate during heavy traffic
When vehicle is disabled, stopped on shoulder, or warning of an obstacle
To claim temporary loading privileges in clearly marked municipal fire zones

questions.statutory_rationale: Four-way emergency hazard flashers are designed to warn other motorists of a vehicular traffic hazard, disabled vehicle, or unexpected road obstruction.

questions.prompt: Does activating a turn signal grant a driver the legal right-of-way to change lanes on a Texas highway?

options.text: Yes, adjacent drivers must immediately yield once any turn signal flashes
Yes, but exclusively when changing into the designated left carpool lane
Only if the turn signal has been active for longer than five full seconds
No, a signal merely indicates intent; the driver must verify lane is clear

questions.statutory_rationale: Signaling communicates intention, but never confers right-of-way. The merging driver must yield to vehicles already occupying the lane and move only when safe.

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §547.501, what distance must a motor vehicle horn be audible under normal conditions?

options.text: Audible under normal conditions from a distance of at least 200 feet
Audible under normal conditions from a distance of at least 50 feet
Audible under normal conditions from a distance of at least 500 feet
Audible under normal conditions from a distance of at least 1,000 feet

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §547.501 mandates that a motor vehicle horn shall emit a sound audible under normal conditions from a distance of at least 200 feet, used only for safety warnings.

topic_title: Passing, Turning, Stopping & Parking Laws

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.057, when is passing another vehicle on the right legally permitted?

options.text: Whenever driving on an unpaved rural road shoulder at high cruising speed
When the overtaken vehicle is making a left turn and pavement permits
Whenever traffic is congested and shoulder driving saves commuting time
Passing on the right is never permitted under any circumstances in Texas

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.057, passing on the right is permitted when the vehicle overtaken is making or about to make a left turn, without driving off the main traveled pavement.

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.302, what is the minimum legal parking clearance from a fire hydrant?

options.text: At least 10 feet from the fire hydrant curb location
At least 20 feet from the fire hydrant curb location
At least 15 feet from the fire hydrant curb location
At least 30 feet from the fire hydrant curb location

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.302(b)(1), an operator may not stand or park a vehicle within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, ensuring emergency fire engines have unobstructed access.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum legal distance a driver may park from an intersection stop sign or flashing beacon?

options.text: At least 15 feet from the nearest curb edge of the intersection
At least 20 feet from the crosswalk or intersection cross street
At least 50 feet from the roadway edge of any nearby railroad rail
At least 30 feet upon the approach to any flashing signal or stop sign

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.302(b)(4), an operator may not park within 30 feet upon the approach to any flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign, or traffic-control signal.

questions.prompt: Why does Texas Transportation Code §545.406 prohibit coasting with transmission in neutral down hills?

options.text: Coasting in neutral reduces vehicle steering and engine braking control
Coasting in neutral increases vehicle tailpipe emissions beyond limits
Coasting in neutral causes immediate failure of vehicle transmission gears
Coasting in neutral disables electronic antilock braking sensor systems

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.406 prohibits coasting in neutral on a downgrade because engine braking is lost, resulting in rapid brake overheating and reduced emergency vehicle control.

questions.prompt: When parking facing uphill along a curbed street, how must the front wheels be positioned for safety?

options.text: Turned sharply toward the curb so the front tire rests flush against edge
Turned sharply away from the curb so the rear edge rolls into curb if rolling
Straightened parallel to the roadway lane with parking brake disengaged
Turned left or right at random provided the manual gear shifter is in park

questions.statutory_rationale: When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb (toward the street center) so that if brakes fail, the back of the front tire rolls against the curb and stops.

topic_title: Defining & Avoiding Blind Spot Driving

questions.prompt: How far does the rear blind spot (No-Zone) extend behind a large commercial freight tractor-trailer?

options.text: Up to 50 feet directly behind the trailer where the driver cannot see you
Up to 500 feet directly behind the trailer where the driver cannot see you
Up to 200 feet directly behind the trailer where the driver cannot see you
Commercial trucks have zero rear blind spots due to wide convex mirrors

questions.statutory_rationale: The rear blind spot of an 18-wheeler extends up to 200 feet behind the trailer. If you follow closely, the driver cannot see you and you lose forward sight distance.

questions.prompt: How does the Blind Spot & Glare Elimination (BGE) mirror setting reduce roadway lane-change risk?

options.text: By tilting mirrors downward toward the road pavement to monitor tire wear
By angling side mirrors inward to see the entire side of your own vehicle
By adjusting the interior rearview mirror exclusively toward rear passengers
By angling side mirrors outward fifteen degrees to overlap peripheral vision

questions.statutory_rationale: BGE settings turn side mirrors outward approximately 15 degrees so cars leaving the center rearview mirror appear immediately in the side mirror, eliminating blind spots.

questions.statute: TX TRANS CODE §545.060 / TX DRIVER HANDBOOK CH. 6
questions.prompt: During a lane change, why is a physical over-the-shoulder chin-to-shoulder head check mandatory?

options.text: To verify vehicles or motorcycles hidden in mirror blind spots before moving
To stretch neck vertebrae and relieve physiological highway fatigue
To ensure rear-seat passengers have secured their lap safety belt buckles
To verify that the vehicle's rear turn signal bulb is actively flashing

questions.statutory_rationale: Mirrors cannot eliminate every blind angle, especially for narrow profiles like motorcycles or bicycles. A quick shoulder check confirms the adjacent space is clear.

questions.prompt: Why is cruising alongside another vehicle in their blind spot considered high-risk driving behavior?

options.text: It causes mutual electromagnetic interference between modern GPS receivers
If that driver swerves to avoid a road hazard, they will steer into your car
It doubles the rate of fuel consumption for both adjacent vehicles traveling
It violates Texas commercial axle weight restrictions on interstate roads

questions.statutory_rationale: Lingering in a blind spot deprives both drivers of an escape route. If the other driver swerves or changes lanes without looking, a side-swipe collision is inevitable.

questions.prompt: Which side of a commercial truck contains the largest and most dangerous blind spot corridor?

options.text: The left side directly adjacent to the driver's exterior side window
The front bumper extending exactly two feet beyond the radiator grill
The right side, extending across three lanes and backwards along trailer
Both sides possess identical symmetrical blind spots of thirty feet

questions.statutory_rationale: Because the driver sits on the left, the right-side blind spot is substantially larger, extending across multiple lanes. Passing on the right of a truck is extremely hazardous.

topic_title: Establishing a Safe Following Interval (3-Sec Rule)

questions.prompt: How does a Texas motorist accurately measure a three-second following distance interval?

options.text: Measure sixty feet of pavement distance for every fifteen miles per hour
Glance at the digital vehicle speedometer every three seconds in heavy traffic
Maintain two car lengths of distance for each passenger riding in your vehicle
Count seconds after the lead car passes a roadside landmark until your car passes

questions.statutory_rationale: Select a fixed overhead sign or pole. When the lead vehicle passes it, count 'one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three'. Your car should not pass the mark before three.

questions.prompt: What following interval does the Texas driver education curriculum mandate at speeds exceeding 30 mph?

options.text: Maintain a minimum of four seconds following distance behind lead vehicles
Maintain a minimum of two seconds following distance behind lead vehicles
Maintain a minimum of one second following distance behind lead vehicles
Maintain a minimum of ten seconds following distance behind lead vehicles

questions.statutory_rationale: While 2 seconds is acceptable under 30 mph in city driving, speeds above 30 mph demand at least 4 seconds following interval, and 4 seconds is best practice for new drivers.

questions.prompt: Why must you increase following distance to four to six seconds when following a motorcycle?

options.text: Motorcycle exhaust pipes emit heavy combustible gasses that ignite car radiators
Motorcycles can stop much faster than cars, and minor contact is fatal to rider
Texas law requires passenger cars to yield right-of-way to all two-wheeled units
Motorcycle riders possess statutory rights to occupy two full adjacent lanes

questions.statutory_rationale: Motorcycles have excellent braking capabilities and can stop in much shorter distances than passenger cars. Following closely creates severe risk of running over the rider.

questions.prompt: What is the average driver perception and reaction time when confronting an unexpected road hazard?

options.text: Approximately 0.25 seconds to perceive danger and depress the brake pedal
Approximately 3.50 seconds to perceive danger and depress the brake pedal
Approximately 1.50 seconds to perceive danger and depress the brake pedal
Approximately 5.00 seconds to perceive danger and depress the brake pedal

questions.statutory_rationale: Average perception time (0.75s) plus reaction time (0.75s) totals approximately 1.5 seconds. At 50 mph, your car travels 109 feet during this 1.5 seconds before brakes even engage.

questions.prompt: When stopped behind a motorcycle at a red light, how much space buffer should you maintain?

options.text: Within eighteen inches of the rear motorcycle tire to maximize road capacity
Two inches from the motorcycle exhaust pipe to keep traffic flowing compact
Pull directly abreast of the motorcycle inside the same lane at crosswalk
A full vehicle length buffer to prevent pushing rider into traffic if struck

questions.statutory_rationale: Maintain at least a full vehicle length behind a stopped motorcycle. If your vehicle is rear-ended from behind, this buffer prevents crushing the vulnerable rider.

topic_title: Speed Related to Stopping & Roadway Conditions

questions.prompt: When a vehicle's cruising speed doubles from 30 mph to 60 mph, how does its braking distance change?

options.text: Braking distance increases by four times because energy quadruples with speed
Braking distance doubles in direct proportion to the increase in road speed
Braking distance triples due to moderate mechanical heating of brake shoes
Braking distance remains identical provided the antilock brakes operate

questions.statutory_rationale: Kinetic energy equals 1/2 m v^2. When speed doubles, kinetic energy increases by 2 squared (4 times). Therefore, it takes four times more distance to stop the car.

questions.prompt: Under good road conditions, what is the total stopping distance for a passenger car traveling at 50 mph?

options.text: Approximately 75 feet total stopping distance including reaction time
Approximately 229 feet total stopping distance including reaction time
Approximately 450 feet total stopping distance including reaction time
Approximately 120 feet total stopping distance including reaction time

questions.statutory_rationale: At 50 mph, driver reaction distance is approximately 109 feet (at 1.5s) and vehicle braking distance is 120 feet, totaling approximately 229 feet to stop completely.

questions.prompt: What is the legal minimum tire tread depth required for passenger motor vehicles operating in Texas?

options.text: At least 4/32 inch of tread depth across all major center tire grooves
At least 1/16 inch of tread depth measured on the outer tire sidewall
At least 2/32 inch of tread depth in all major grooves of road contact
Tires may be completely bald provided the inner steel belt is unexposed

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §547.612 and Texas safety inspection standards require at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. Tires below 2/32 inch cannot evacuate water and hydroplane easily.

questions.prompt: How does driving on wet asphalt pavement affect passenger vehicle braking stopping distance?

options.text: Wet pavement decreases braking distance because water cools the brake drums
Wet pavement has zero impact on stopping distance with electronic brakes
Wet pavement cuts total stopping distance in half due to hydrodynamic tire grip
Wet pavement can double stopping distance and drastically reduce tire grip

questions.statutory_rationale: Water reduces pavement coefficient of friction by 50% or more, doubling braking distance. Drivers must reduce speed and extend following distances accordingly.

questions.prompt: In an emergency stop with Antilock Braking Systems (ABS), what is the correct driver pedal technique?

options.text: Stomp firmly on brake pedal, stay hard on pedal, and steer around hazard
Pump the brake pedal vigorously up and down to prevent brake lockup
Shift transmission quickly into neutral and pull the emergency parking brake
Tap the pedal gently three times and release steering wheel control completely

questions.statutory_rationale: With ABS, remember 'Stomp, Stay, and Steer': stomp hard on the pedal, hold firm continuous pressure despite pulsating sensations, and steer toward safety.

topic_title: Adjusting Speed for Poor Weather & Flash Floods

questions.prompt: How little moving water across a Texas low-water crossing is capable of carrying away a vehicle?

options.text: At least four feet of rushing floodwater before vehicles lose tire traction
Twelve to twenty-four inches of water can float and carry away passenger cars
Only ocean storm surges exceeding ten feet can move standard passenger trucks
Six feet of deep flowing current is required to overcome heavy vehicle weight

questions.statutory_rationale: Just 6 inches of water stalls cars and can sweep pedestrians off their feet; 12 to 24 inches (1 to 2 feet) will float and carry away most passenger cars, SUVs, and trucks.

questions.prompt: What are the legal criminal penalties under Texas Transportation Code §472.022 for driving around a flood barricade?

options.text: A standard parking citation with a ten-dollar municipal court administrative fee
Mandatory forfeiture of all personal motor vehicles to the Texas Department of Public Safety
Class B misdemeanor punishable by fines up to $1,000 and up to 180 days in jail
Immediate permanent revocation of driving privileges with no right of administrative appeal

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §472.022, driving around a barricade erected for flooding is a Class B misdemeanor (fines up to $1,000 and/or jail up to 180 days, escalating if bodily injury occurs).

questions.prompt: At what speeds can passenger vehicles begin to hydroplane on water-covered Texas roadways?

options.text: Hydroplaning occurs exclusively at high speeds exceeding ninety miles per hour
Tires cannot hydroplane unless all four tires possess less than 1/32 inch tread
Only commercial 18-wheel tractor-trailers can hydroplane on standing puddles
Hydroplaning can begin at speeds as low as thirty-five miles per hour in rain

questions.statutory_rationale: Hydroplaning occurs when water builds in front of tires faster than the tread can channel it away. It can begin at speeds as low as 35 mph, with complete loss of traction at 55 mph.

questions.prompt: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane across standing water, what is the proper emergency recovery action?

options.text: Ease foot off the accelerator, avoid braking, and steer straight ahead
Slam hard on the emergency brakes and turn the steering wheel lock-to-lock
Downshift rapidly into first gear and pump accelerator pedal to clear water
Engage cruise control to maintain consistent wheel rotation through puddle

questions.statutory_rationale: Do not slam on brakes or steer abruptly. Ease off the gas pedal to let the vehicle decelerate naturally until tires regain contact with the pavement surface.

questions.prompt: Why are Texas highways most dangerously slick during the first twenty to thirty minutes of rainfall?

options.text: Asphalt road temperature drops instantly by forty degrees causing surface freeze
Rainwater mixes with accumulated motor oil and grime creating an oily film
Highway electronic speed limit display signs temporarily turn off for safety
Tire rubber expands rapidly in the first minutes of rain reducing traction

questions.statutory_rationale: During dry spells, oil, grease, and exhaust grime build up on the road. When light rain starts, it mixes with these residues to form an extremely slick emulsion before washing away.

topic_title: Legal Speed Limits for Texas Roadways & Beaches

questions.prompt: What is the statutory prima facie speed limit in a Texas urban district unless otherwise posted?

Forty-five miles per hour in urban districts and residential neighborhood streets
Thirty miles per hour in urban districts and residential neighborhood streets
Fifty miles per hour in urban districts and residential neighborhood streets

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.352(b)(1), the statutory prima facie speed limit in an urban district is 30 miles per hour unless altered by municipal authority.

questions.prompt: What is the legal maximum speed limit when driving along public Texas ocean beaches or urban alleys?

options.text: Twenty-five miles per hour along public beaches and urban alley corridors
Thirty miles per hour along public beaches and urban alley corridors
Ten miles per hour along public beaches and urban alley corridors
Fifteen miles per hour along public beaches and urban alley corridors

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.352(b)(2), the prima facie speed limit on an alley or adjacent to a public beach is 15 miles per hour to protect pedestrians and beachfront visitors.

questions.prompt: What is the statutory speed limit for passenger vehicles on numbered state highways outside urban districts?

options.text: Seventy miles per hour (uniform day and night limit under current Texas law)
Fifty-five miles per hour during day and forty-five miles per hour at night
Sixty-five miles per hour unless driving on an interstate highway corridor
Eighty-five miles per hour on all two-lane farm-to-market numbered roadways

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.352, the statutory speed limit is 70 mph on numbered highways outside urban areas. In 2011, Texas repealed lower nighttime speed limits, making daytime and night limits uniform.

questions.prompt: What is the highest legal posted speed limit authorized anywhere on the Texas state highway system?

options.text: Seventy-five miles per hour on designated interstate freeway segments
Eighty-five miles per hour on designated toll roads like State Highway 130
Eighty miles per hour on rural interstate corridors in West Texas counties
Ninety miles per hour on limited-access state toll road facilities

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.353 authorizes TxDOT to post speed limits up to 85 mph on highways designed to accommodate that speed (e.g., portions of State Highway 130 toll road).

questions.prompt: Under what authority can minimum speed limit signs (e.g. 45 MPH) be established on Texas freeways?

options.text: Private trucking companies to ensure commercial freight arrival schedules
Homeowner associations along neighborhood collector street thoroughfares
TxDOT and local authorities when slow speeds consistently impede flow and safety
Minimum speed limits are unconstitutional and prohibited throughout Texas

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.363, the Texas Transportation Commission or local authorities may declare a minimum speed limit when engineering studies show slow speeds impede normal traffic.

topic_title: Law and Purpose of Vehicle Lighting Equipment

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §547.302, when must a driver display lighted vehicle lamps?

From one hour after sunset until one hour before sunrise in rural areas
Only when rain or fog reduces forward sight distance below one hundred feet
From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or if visibility < 1000 ft

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §547.302 mandates lighted headlamps at nighttime (30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise) and whenever persons/vehicles are not discernable for 1,000 feet.

questions.prompt: At what distance must you dim your high-beam headlights when approaching an oncoming vehicle in Texas?

Within 200 feet of an oncoming vehicle approaching from opposite direction
Within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle approaching from opposite direction
Within 100 feet of an oncoming vehicle approaching from opposite direction

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §547.333(c)(1) mandates dimming high-beam headlamps whenever an operator approaches an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet.

questions.prompt: What is the mandatory dimming distance when following behind another vehicle traveling in your lane?

options.text: Dim high beams within 100 feet when following another vehicle from behind
Dim high beams within 300 feet when following another vehicle from behind
Dim high beams within 500 feet when following another vehicle from behind
Dim high beams within 50 feet when following another vehicle from behind

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §547.333(c)(2), an operator following another vehicle within 300 feet to the rear must use low-beam lighting to prevent blinding the lead driver via mirrors.

questions.prompt: Is it legal to operate a motor vehicle on Texas roadways with only parking lights illuminated at dusk?

options.text: Yes, parking lights provide adequate illumination for municipal city driving
Yes, but only if the vehicle travels below twenty-five miles per hour
No, driving with only parking lights on when lights are required is illegal
Yes, parking lights are legally interchangeable with standard low beams

questions.statutory_rationale: Parking lights are for parking only. Operating a moving vehicle with only parking lights illuminated when headlights are required violates Texas vehicle equipment law.

questions.prompt: Why should drivers use low beams or specialized fog lamps rather than high beams during heavy fog?

options.text: High beams consume excessive electrical alternator wattage in cold moist air
Fog droplets will fracture the glass lenses of halogen high-beam bulbs
High beams are illegal on Texas state roadways whenever fog is present
High beams reflect off airborne fog water droplets, blinding the driver with glare

questions.statutory_rationale: High beams project light upward into water droplets, reflecting light back into the driver's eyes. Low beams project light down toward the pavement surface, illuminating the lane.

topic_title: Freeway Entry, Travel & Exit Procedures

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.154, what is the right-of-way rule for entering a controlled-access freeway?

Entering vehicles have absolute right-of-way over freeway travel lanes
Entering vehicles and freeway vehicles must stop alternately in turn
Freeway drivers are legally required to change lanes to let on-ramps enter

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.154, an operator on an access or feeder ramp entering a freeway or controlled-access highway shall yield right-of-way to vehicles on the highway main lanes.

questions.prompt: What is the proper driver technique when traveling along a freeway entrance acceleration lane?

options.text: Come to a complete stop at the start of the ramp and look for traffic gaps
Accelerate to match freeway traffic speed, find a safe gap, and merge smoothly
Drive at fifteen miles per hour until reaching the end of the merge stripe
Sound the vehicle horn continuously to force highway traffic into median

questions.statutory_rationale: Use the ramp and acceleration lane to accelerate to the cruising speed of freeway traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge smoothly into an open gap.

questions.prompt: In a shared weaving lane where vehicles are entering and exiting simultaneously, who yields right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle entering the freeway has right-of-way over exiting traffic
The larger commercial transport vehicle always takes statutory right-of-way
The vehicle exiting the freeway has right-of-way over entering traffic
Both vehicles must come to an immediate halt until traffic passes by

questions.statutory_rationale: By standard highway convention and safety rules, the exiting vehicle (leaving high-speed traffic) is given priority, while the entering vehicle yields and adjusts position.

questions.prompt: If you inadvertently miss your intended exit ramp on a Texas freeway, what is the required legal action?

options.text: Shift into reverse on the paved shoulder and back up to the missed exit
Make a tight U-turn across the paved median opening between lanes
Stop in the right travel lane and wait for an opening to cut across ramp
Proceed forward to the next authorized exit and reroute safely via streets

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.415, backing on a controlled-access highway shoulder or roadway is illegal. Drivers who miss an exit must proceed to the next exit and safely double back.

questions.prompt: When a Texas highway displays 'LEFT LANE FOR PASSING ONLY' signs, how may drivers use the left lane?

options.text: Left lane is reserved strictly for overtaking and passing slower traffic
Left lane may be used for continuous cruising if driving at the speed limit
Left lane is designated exclusively for commercial diesel tractor-trailers
Left lane may be used whenever the driver desires to avoid merge ramps

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.051, when signed 'Left Lane For Passing Only', it is a traffic violation to cruise in the left lane; it may only be used for passing or making a left exit.

topic_title: Avoiding Fatigue Driving & Highway Hypnosis

questions.prompt: What is 'highway hypnosis' and under what conditions does it typically affect long-distance drivers?

options.text: An allergic respiratory reaction triggered by highway vehicle exhaust fumes
A trance-like state of dulled awareness caused by monotonous highway driving
Sudden visual blindness caused by intense afternoon sun glare on asphalt
Muscle paralysis of the legs resulting from poorly adjusted driver seating

questions.statutory_rationale: Highway hypnosis is a drowsy, trance-like state resulting from staring at monotonous unbroken road lines for long periods, severely dulling alertness and reaction time.

questions.prompt: What schedule of rest stops does the Texas driver education curriculum recommend on long trips?

options.text: Drive continuously for eight hours without stopping to reach destination
Stop only when the vehicle low-fuel dashboard warning light illuminates
Stop for a fifteen-minute rest break every two hours or every 100 miles
Take a thirty-minute break exclusively after completing 500 highway miles

questions.statutory_rationale: Take a 15-minute rest break every 2 hours or every 100 miles. Walk around, get fresh air, stretch muscles, and let your eyes rest from staring at highway lanes.

questions.prompt: What occurs during a driver 'microsleep' episode while traveling at sixty-five miles per hour?

options.text: The vehicle's electronic cruise control automatically disengages the throttle
The driver experiences enhanced peripheral vision and heightened reflexes
The driver blinks rapidly twenty times without losing roadway awareness
The driver sleeps for three to five seconds, traveling hundreds of feet blind

questions.statutory_rationale: A microsleep lasts 3 to 5 seconds. At 65 mph, your vehicle travels roughly 100 feet per second—meaning you travel the length of an entire football field completely unconscious.

questions.prompt: Why are rolling down windows, turning up loud music, or drinking coffee ineffective cures for fatigue?

options.text: They provide only brief sensory stimulation; the underlying sleep deficit remains
They cause rapid vehicle battery discharge while operating high-speed travel
They are classified as moving infractions under the Texas Transportation Code
They decrease blood circulation to the brain, inducing deeper somnolence

questions.statutory_rationale: Sensory tricks mask sleepiness for only a few minutes. The brain remains severely sleep-deprived, and reaction times remain degraded. Real sleep is the only cure.

questions.prompt: During what biological clock hours are fatigue-related crashes most statistically prevalent in Texas?

options.text: Between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM during peak morning suburban commute rush hours
Between 12:00 AM and 6:00 AM, and during the afternoon lull between 2:00 PM and 4:00 PM
Between 5:00 PM and 7:00 PM during evening homebound traffic congestion
Fatigue crashes are distributed perfectly evenly across all twenty-four hours

questions.statutory_rationale: The human body circadian cycle experiences natural alertness dips between midnight and 6:00 AM, and a secondary circadian drop between 2:00 PM and 4:00 PM.

topic_title: Managing Roadside Vehicle Breakdowns Safely

questions.prompt: If your vehicle breaks down on a high-speed Texas highway, where must you position the disabled car?

options.text: Stop immediately in the center lane and place orange cones around trunk
Leave vehicle resting diagonally across the left-hand passing lane median
Pull completely off paved travel lanes onto the right shoulder or grassy berm
Stop at the entrance of an on-ramp where tow trucks can spot you easily

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.301, stopping on the main traveled portion of a highway is prohibited. Drivers must pull completely off the roadway onto the right shoulder.

questions.prompt: How should a stranded driver signal roadside distress while awaiting assistance on a highway?

options.text: Stand in the adjacent traffic travel lane and wave both arms over your head
Lay down on the hood of the vehicle with a flashlight pointed at the sky
Walk down the center median barrier waving an unlit flare towards traffic
Turn on four-way flashers, raise the hood, or tie a white cloth to door handle

questions.statutory_rationale: Activate hazard lights, raise the hood, and tie a white cloth or paper to the driver door handle or antenna to indicate to DPS troopers and passing drivers that help is needed.

questions.prompt: Why should stranded occupants remain inside a disabled vehicle with seatbelts buckled on highway shoulders?

options.text: Standing outside exposes pedestrians to fatal impacts from errant highway vehicles
Texas law fines pedestrians who exit vehicles on state highways twenty dollars
Vehicle electrical computers discharge faster when passenger doors are opened
To prevent unauthorized entry by roadside stray livestock along rural roads

questions.statutory_rationale: Standing on a highway shoulder is exceptionally hazardous; dozens of stranded motorists are struck and killed each year. The vehicle cabin and seatbelts offer structural protection.

questions.prompt: When placing emergency reflective warning triangles behind a disabled vehicle, what is safe placement?

options.text: Stack all three triangles directly on the vehicle trunk lid next to the rear window
Place triangles 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind car to warn oncoming traffic
Place triangles along the opposite side of the highway across median barrier
Place all triangles within three feet of the front bumper facing traffic

questions.statutory_rationale: Place one triangle 10 feet directly behind, a second 100 feet back on the shoulder, and a third 200 feet back (especially if approaching over a hill crest or curve).

questions.prompt: What should you do if your flat tire is on the left side facing high-speed traffic lanes on a narrow shoulder?

options.text: Kneel in the travel lane and change the tire as rapidly as humanly possible
Ask passengers to stand in the traffic lane to wave speeding cars away
Do not attempt to change it; call professional roadside assistance or tow truck
Roll the vehicle onto the center yellow rumble strip to complete the job

questions.statutory_rationale: Never work on the traffic side of a vehicle on a narrow shoulder. The risk of being clipped by passing vehicles is catastrophic. Call a tow truck or DPS for a lane cushion.

topic_title: Emergency Control: Skids, Blowouts & Brake Failure

questions.prompt: If the rear wheels of your vehicle lose traction and skid to the right, how should you steer to recover?

options.text: Slam hard on the service brakes and turn the steering wheel sharply left
Floor the gas accelerator pedal and pull the manual emergency handbrake
Hold steering wheel rigidly straight and shift transmission to reverse
Ease off gas, avoid slamming brakes, and steer smoothly to the right into skid

questions.statutory_rationale: Take your foot off the gas and avoid sudden braking. Steer in the direction of the skid (if the rear slides right, steer right). As the car straightens, straighten wheels.

questions.prompt: What is the proper driver response when a front tire blows out at sixty miles per hour on a highway?

options.text: Grip steering wheel firmly, maintain straight path, ease off gas, brake gently
Slam immediately on the brakes and steer aggressively toward the ditch
Shift transmission instantly into park to lock front wheel rotation
Accelerate heavily to generate centrifugal force to reinflate tire carcass

questions.statutory_rationale: A blowout pulls hard toward the flat tire. Grip the wheel firmly with both hands, keep vehicle straight, ease off the accelerator, and brake gently only after control is stabilized.

questions.prompt: If your service brake pedal sinks completely to the floorboards without stopping, what initial action should you take?

options.text: Turn off vehicle ignition key immediately to lock steering column in place
Pump brake pedal rapidly to rebuild hydraulic pressure and downshift to lower gear
Shift quickly to reverse to force engine rotation to counter momentum
Climb into passenger seat and wait for friction to halt the rolling chassis

questions.statutory_rationale: Rapid pumping can build enough residual hydraulic pressure to stop. Simultaneously downshift to a lower gear to use engine braking, and apply parking brake gradually.

questions.prompt: If your right wheels drop off the paved road onto a low shoulder, how should you return to the highway?

options.text: Jerk steering wheel hard to the left immediately while braking hard
Accelerate rapidly and steer into the ditch to bounce back onto asphalt
Hold wheel straight, ease off gas, slow down, check traffic, steer back smoothly
Pull the emergency parking brake lever immediately while turning wheels

questions.statutory_rationale: Jerking the wheel causes rollover or catapults the car into oncoming traffic. Hold straight, ease off the gas, slow to under 25 mph, check traffic, and ease back onto pavement.

questions.prompt: If the vehicle accelerator pedal jams wide open at highway speeds, what is the safest immediate action?

options.text: Turn ignition key completely to off position and remove key from cylinder

Bridges are constructed from reflective steel metals that attract frost flakes
Underground geothermal heat warms standard highway pavement from below
Elevated bridges are positioned closer to cloud formations and ice crystals

It is ultra-thin and transparent, appearing merely as innocent wet pavement
It forms exclusively during hot summer months on newly surfaced asphalt
It disables modern vehicle antilock braking electronic circuit boards

Decrease following distance to one second to stay within tracks of lead car
Increase following interval to at least six to ten seconds behind other traffic
Follow at precisely thirty feet regardless of highway cruising travel speed

Predictability eliminates the legal requirement to carry minimum auto insurance

Mandatory off-road detours across unpaved pastureland access tracks

An alcohol concentration of 0.02 or more in blood, breath, or urine sample

Driving five miles per hour under the posted highway speed limit at night

0.06 BAC when operating tractor-trailers during nighttime delivery hours

Approximately two standard drinks per hour when exercising vigorously outdoors
The liver eliminates all consumed alcohol immediately within twenty-five minutes

Accelerated liver filtering, clearing both substances from the body much faster

Temporary immunity from field sobriety eye nystagmus examination detections

Color perception when reading red and green illuminated intersection signals
Judgment, reasoning ability, and risk assessment are impaired first by alcohol

Consuming greasy high-carbohydrate fast foods immediately before driving

Has zero impact on vision provided the driver wears corrective eyeglass lenses

Pedestrians, bicyclists, roadside construction workers, and motorcycle riders

questions.statutory_rationale: Vulnerable road users lack the protective structural metal cage and airbags of passenger cars. They include pedestrians, cyclists, workers, and motorcyclists.

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §552.003, when must a driver yield right-of-way to a pedestrian in a crosswalk?

options.text: When the pedestrian is on the half of the roadway on which the vehicle is traveling
Only when the pedestrian holds an illuminated handheld warning torch
Only if the pedestrian is crossing within an active public school zone corridor
Pedestrians must always yield to motorized vehicular traffic in crosswalks

Take all necessary precautions, come to a complete stop, and yield right-of-way
Proceed at standard speed if your travel lane displays a solid green light
Direct the pedestrian verbally through open driver window to cross street

questions.statutory_rationale: Under Texas Human Resources Code §121.007, an operator approaching a blind person carrying a predominantly white cane or using a guide dog must take necessary precautions to avoid injury and stop.

questions.prompt: What type of vehicle is required to display a reflective triangular Slow-Moving Vehicle (SMV) emblem in Texas?

options.text: All student driver training vehicles operating on multi-lane highways
Commercial garbage disposal trucks collecting municipal residential waste
Any vehicle or farm tractor designed to operate at speeds of 25 mph or less
Passenger hybrid electric vehicles driving in high-occupancy vehicle lanes

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §547.008, vehicles designed to operate at a maximum speed of 25 mph or less (such as tractors, farm equipment, and construction machinery) must display an SMV triangular emblem.

questions.prompt: Why are motorcycles exceptionally vulnerable to severe collisions at intersections in Texas?

options.text: Motorcycles are legally exempt from obeying municipal traffic stop signs
Motorcycle braking systems require four times longer distance to stop
Motorcycle engines emit low-frequency sounds that jam radar detectors
Their narrow silhouette is easily hidden in vehicle blind spots or misjudged

questions.statutory_rationale: Motorcycles have a narrow profile that makes estimating their speed and distance difficult. Drivers frequently turn left across their path claiming 'I didn't see them'.

Drive to the nearest municipal police station within forty-eight hours to report
Continue home and notify automobile insurance adjusters via mobile website
Leave personal contact information on a note attached to the street sign

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §550.021, an operator involved in an accident resulting in injury or death must immediately stop, determine if aid is required, provide information, and remain at the scene.

questions.prompt: What is the criminal penalty under Texas law for fleeing the scene of a crash resulting in a fatality?

options.text: Class C misdemeanor settled by paying a five-hundred-dollar traffic ticket
Second-degree felony punishable by 2 to 20 years in prison and fines up to $10,000
Civil administrative penalty involving thirty days community work service
State jail misdemeanor carrying up to forty-five days in county detention

questions.prompt: How does the Texas Good Samaritan Law protect citizens who administer emergency first aid at crash scenes?

options.text: Compensates rescuers with cash payments from state treasury emergency funds
Provides automatic immunity from all future state moving traffic violations
Shields citizens from civil damages for emergency care rendered in good faith
Authorizes untrained citizens to perform complex field surgical operations

questions.prompt: What specific information must motorists exchange following a vehicle crash in Texas?

options.text: Personal social security number, home mortgage papers, and tax returns
Digital passwords to personal cell phones and vehicle navigation memory
Complete employment medical records and blood laboratory test results
Operator name, address, vehicle registration, and liability insurance details

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §550.023 requires providing name, address, vehicle registration number, showing driver license upon request, and providing liability insurer information.

questions.prompt: If you strike an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what does Texas law require?

options.text: Attach a secure, plainly visible written note giving your name, address, and insurer
Leave the scene immediately if vehicle damage is estimated under $5,000
Wait for twenty-four hours next to the struck vehicle until the owner returns
Sound your vehicle horn repeatedly until surrounding neighborhood residents exit

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §550.024, if you strike an unattended vehicle, you must locate the owner or leave in a conspicuous place a written notice giving your name, address, and statement of circumstances.

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §551.101, what legal status and rights do bicyclists hold on roadways?

Bicyclists have all rights and duties applicable to motor vehicle drivers
Bicycles may only operate on sidewalks and are banned from all city streets
Bicyclists are legally required to ride facing against oncoming traffic

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §551.101 states that a person operating a bicycle has the rights and duties applicable to a driver operating a motor vehicle, including obeying traffic signs and signals.

One foot of clearance while sounding your vehicle horn continuously
At least three feet of lateral clearance (six feet for commercial trucks)
Motorists must never pass bicyclists; they must follow at bicycle speed

questions.statutory_rationale: Safe passing laws and TDLR driver standards mandate giving bicyclists at least 3 feet of lateral clearance when passing (and 6 feet for commercial vehicles), or changing lanes when safe.

questions.prompt: What is commercial truck 'off-tracking' and why does it endanger motorists during turns?

options.text: Commercial truck tires slide sideways whenever traveling across bridge decks
The electronic satellite navigation system loses tracking in rural regions
Truck cargo shifts balance rapidly, tipping the trailer into oncoming lanes
Rear trailer wheels track closer to the curb than front wheels during turns

questions.statutory_rationale: In a turn, trailer wheels follow a shorter path than the cab (off-tracking). A truck turning right may swing wide left first; cutting into the right-hand gap results in being crushed.

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.308, what is the required conduct when encountering horseback riders?

options.text: Reduce speed, do not sound horn or rev engine, and pass with extreme caution
Sound your horn repeatedly to alert the animal of your approaching vehicle
Accelerate quickly to clear the corridor before the animal enters the lane
Animals are illegal on Texas state roadways and drivers owe zero duties

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.308, ridden animals have the rights of vehicles. Honking or revving engines can spook a horse, causing it to bolt into traffic or throw its rider.

questions.prompt: When driving adjacent to urban light rail tracks in Dallas or Houston, what is strictly prohibited?

options.text: Operating windshield wipers within one hundred feet of an overhead rail line
Stopping, standing, or parking on transit tracks or turning across train paths
Listening to car stereo audio broadcasts while traveling near rail stations
Changing headlights to low beams while driving parallel to train tracks

questions.statutory_rationale: Light rail trains move rapidly and cannot stop quickly or steer away. Never stop on rail tracks, never attempt to beat a train, and obey transit signals explicitly.

topic_title: Responsibilities of a Defensive Driver — IPDE Process

questions.prompt: What are the four systematic stages of the IPDE defensive driving decision-making process?

options.text: Inspect vehicle fluids, Park smoothly, Decelerate gently, Exit calmly
Ignite motor engine, Push gas pedal, Downshift transmission, Engage clutch
Identify roadway hazards, Predict consequences, Decide actions, Execute safely
Inform passengers, Practice maneuvers, Deflect criticism, Evaluate fines

questions.statutory_rationale: The IPDE process is the core defensive driving strategy: Identify clues in the driving environment, Predict how hazards could develop, Decide what action to take, and Execute smoothly.

questions.prompt: How far ahead should a defensive driver look to predict hazards along Texas thoroughfares?

options.text: Directly at the rear taillights of the car immediately ahead of your bumper
Exclusively 2 seconds ahead to preserve optical retinal focus from strain
Look only into the rearview mirror every twenty seconds during cruise travel
At least 12 to 15 seconds ahead in city streets and 20 to 30 seconds on highways

questions.statutory_rationale: Maintaining a visual lead of 12-15 seconds in urban driving and 20-30 seconds on highways allows drivers to detect hazards early and plan actions before an emergency arises.

questions.prompt: When predicting potential hazards in a residential neighborhood, what must a driver anticipate?

options.text: Children darting between parked cars, opening vehicle doors, and pets running
Sudden seismic ground earthquakes cracking residential concrete pavements
Overhead commercial passenger airplanes performing emergency landing glides
Underground municipal water pipeline valves bursting with boiling fluids

questions.statutory_rationale: Defensive driving requires predicting the worst-case scenario: a bouncing ball means a child follows; front wheels turned toward the street mean a parked car may pull out.

questions.prompt: Why should a driver avoid driving in clusters or platoons of vehicles on open Texas highways?

options.text: Clusters increase automated roadside speed radar emission frequencies
Clusters eliminate escape routes, increasing the risk of multi-car pileups
Driving in clusters causes mutual electromagnetic battery discharge rates
Clusters violate Texas commercial freight transportation franchise acts

questions.statutory_rationale: Driving in clusters or packs of cars robs you of space cushions. If one driver brakes or loses control, a cascading multi-car collision is almost unavoidable.

questions.prompt: What psychological trait distinguishes a defensive driver from an aggressive operator?

options.text: Defensive drivers assert legal lane dominance to force others into submission
Defensive drivers use high beams continuously to command intersection path
Defensive drivers accept delays calmly and yield right-of-way to avoid crashes
Defensive drivers follow closely to prevent other motorists from cutting in

questions.statutory_rationale: Defensive driving is built upon patience, humility, and caution. A defensive driver willingly gives up right-of-way if it prevents a collision, prioritizing safety over pride.

Occupants over eighteen years of age traveling on high-speed interstates
Seat belts are optional for rear-seat passengers over the age of fifteen
All vehicle occupants regardless of age or front/rear seating position

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.413, all occupants in a vehicle equipped with safety belts must be secured, regardless of whether they sit in the front or rear seat.

questions.prompt: Until what age and height must children be secured in an approved child safety seat system in Texas?

Until younger than 5 years of age, regardless of physical standing height
Until younger than 12 years of age, unless the child weighs over 100 pounds
Child seats are mandatory only until a toddler reaches their third birthday

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.412 requires child passenger safety seat systems for children younger than 8 years old, unless the child is taller than 4 feet 9 inches (57 inches).

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.414, what is the age restriction for riding in an open pickup truck bed?

options.text: Illegal to operate a truck with a child younger than 12 years riding in the bed
Illegal to operate a truck with a child younger than 18 years riding in the bed
Permitted at all ages provided the truck does not exceed thirty-five mph
Illegal only if traveling on limited-access multi-lane interstate freeways

questions.statutory_rationale: TTC §545.414 makes it a misdemeanor to operate an open-bed pickup truck or open trailer with a passenger under 18 years old in the bed (with narrow agricultural/parade exceptions).

questions.prompt: Under Texas Penal Code §22.10, when is leaving a child unattended inside a motor vehicle a crime?

options.text: Child younger than 12 left unattended for >15 mins while running errands
Only if the outdoor ambient temperature exceeds ninety degrees Fahrenheit
Child younger than 7 left unattended for >5 mins without someone ≥14 years old
Leaving a child inside a parked car is never illegal if windows are cracked

questions.statutory_rationale: TPC §22.10 makes it a Class C misdemeanor to intentionally or knowingly leave a child younger than 7 unattended in a vehicle for longer than 5 minutes without someone at least 14 years old.

questions.prompt: Why can interior vehicle temperatures reach lethal levels within ten minutes in Texas sun?

options.text: Automotive engine blocks radiate excessive residual combustion heat into car
Vehicle battery charging circuits vent high-temperature thermal vapor gases
Cracking side windows causes vacuum currents that draw heated outdoor air
Greenhouse effect traps solar radiation, heating cabin by 20 degrees in 10 mins

questions.statutory_rationale: Cars act like greenhouses. Sunlight heats interiors rapidly, rising nearly 20°F in just 10 minutes and reaching fatal levels (110°F-130°F+) even on mild 70°F days. Cracking windows does not help.

lesson_title: LESSON 07: Sharing the Road & Special Circumstances
topic_title: Responsibilities If Stopped by Law Enforcement

questions.prompt: When a law enforcement officer activates emergency lights behind you, what is the proper pull-over procedure?

options.text: Signal, pull safely to the right shoulder/edge, place in park, and stop
Stop immediately in the center lane and switch off vehicle headlights
Speed up to find a parking lot five miles away without acknowledging lights
Pull sharply onto the left grassy median barrier dividing the highway

questions.statutory_rationale: Signal your intention, slow down, and steer smoothly to the right shoulder or edge of the road, clear of traffic. Place the vehicle in park and set the parking brake.

questions.prompt: What should a driver do immediately after stopping for an officer during a nighttime traffic stop?

options.text: Exit the vehicle immediately and walk toward the patrol cruiser quickly
Turn on interior dome light, roll down driver window, place hands on steering wheel
Reach under passenger seats to search for insurance cards before officer arrives
Rev the engine slightly to verify alternator voltage is charging battery

questions.statutory_rationale: Turn on the interior dome light at night so the officer can see inside. Lower the window and keep both hands visibly placed on the steering wheel (at 10 and 2 or 9 and 3).

questions.prompt: What is the safest protocol when reaching for your driver license and insurance documents during a stop?

options.text: Make sudden fast movements to grab documents before the officer speaks
Refuse to open the glove box unless a municipal search warrant is displayed
Tell the officer where documents are located before reaching into glove box/pocket
Throw the documents out the cracked driver window onto the pavement

questions.statutory_rationale: Always inform the officer where your license and insurance card are located before reaching for them (e.g., 'Officer, my insurance is in the glove compartment; may I reach for it?').

questions.prompt: How should passengers inside a stopped vehicle conduct themselves during a police traffic stop?

options.text: Exit the vehicle immediately and walk into nearby shopping center stores
Argue aggressively with the officer regarding the driver's driving record
Conceal all personal belongings underneath vehicle carpeting and floor mats
Remain seated with hands visible, avoid sudden movements, and follow instructions

questions.statutory_rationale: Passengers should remain calm, stay seated inside the car, keep hands in plain view (e.g., on their laps), avoid unannounced movements, and follow officer directions.

questions.prompt: What does a driver's signature on a Texas traffic citation legally signify?

An agreement to surrender personal vehicle ownership to the municipality
Immediate consent to have points deducted from personal credit bureau scores

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §543.005, signing a traffic citation is merely a promise to appear in court or resolve the citation. It is NOT an admission of guilt. Refusing to sign can result in immediate arrest.

Define mutual rights and expectations during traffic stops to ensure safety
Increase traffic ticket fine revenue collected by county justice courts
Mandate that all high school seniors complete police cadet training camps

May lawfully request driver identification, proof of insurance, and exit of car
Officers have zero legal authority to request passengers to identify themselves

questions.prompt: Does a citizen have the legal right to video record a police traffic stop in Texas?

Recording is permitted exclusively during daylight hours in public park zones
Yes, provided the recording does not physically interfere with officer duties

Physically resist the officer or attempt to drive away from the traffic stop

State greeting, identify themselves and agency, state reason for stop, request ID
Search the vehicle trunk before explaining the reason for the traffic stop
Present the driver with a predetermined hundred-dollar fine payment voucher

lesson_title: LESSON 07: Sharing the Road & Special Circumstances
topic_title: Aggressive Driving & Road Rage Avoidance

questions.prompt: What key distinction separates aggressive driving traffic offenses from criminal 'road rage'?

Road rage applies exclusively to commercial truck drivers on rural interstates
Aggressive driving is moving violations; road rage involves intentional violence
There is zero legal or psychological difference between the two driving terms

questions.statutory_rationale: Aggressive driving involves reckless traffic violations (tailgating, speeding, cutting off). Road rage is a violent criminal act—using a vehicle or weapon to threaten or assault another person.

questions.prompt: What is the most effective defensive action when confronting an enraged, aggressive driver?

options.text: Tap your vehicle brakes suddenly to warn them they are following too close
Roll down your window and explain Texas right-of-way statutes with gestures
Match their highway speed and block them from changing lanes to show control
Avoid eye contact, remain calm, do not gesture, and allow them plenty of room to pass

questions.prompt: If an angry, aggressive driver follows your vehicle and attempts to force you off the road, where should you drive?

options.text: Drive directly to a police station, hospital emergency entrance, or open public place
Drive straight to your personal home garage and lock the overhead door
Pull down an isolated, dark rural unpaved alleyway to lose the tailing car
Stop on the highway shoulder, exit your car, and confront the angry driver

questions.statutory_rationale: Never drive home or to an isolated spot. Call 911 and drive to a police station, fire department, or crowded public facility with security. Never exit your vehicle.

questions.prompt: How should a driver manage their own personal anger or stress before getting behind the wheel?

options.text: Drive aggressively to blow off psychological steam and release anxiety
Recognize emotional distress, delay driving until calm, or take deep breaths
Play high-volume heavy aggressive music and weave through highway lanes
Consume multiple alcoholic energy drinks to suppress nervous tension

questions.statutory_rationale: Driving while furious or distressed impairs judgment as severely as intoxication. Cool off before driving, focus on safety, and remember driving is not a competition.

questions.prompt: What information should you provide to dispatchers when reporting an aggressive driver on a Texas highway?

options.text: Driver's estimated personal household income and automobile loan balance
The manufacturer serial number of the tires installed on the suspect car
Vehicle make/model/color, license plate, highway location, direction, and behavior
Predictions of which exit the aggressive vehicle will take ten miles ahead

questions.statutory_rationale: Call 911 (hands-free or passenger) and report location (highway and mile marker/cross street), travel direction, vehicle description, license plate if possible, and specific actions.

topic_title: Transporting Cargo, Safety Chains & Towing Laws

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.409, how must trailer safety chains be properly attached?

Draped loosely on the ground pavement to discharge static electricity
Attached strictly to the decorative chrome rear bumper license frame
Crossed underneath the trailer tongue to cradle it if the hitch uncouples

questions.prompt: When cargo extends more than 4 feet beyond the rear of a vehicle body, what marking is required?

A handwritten cardboard warning placard attached to rear window wiper
Overhanging loads beyond four feet are strictly prohibited in Texas

options.text: Cargo may be left uncovered provided the truck travels under forty mph
Must be covered with a secure canvas tarp or closed container to prevent blowing
Truck must stop every ten miles to manually shovel loose gravel into center
Covering is required only during nighttime hours between sunset and sunrise

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §725.021, a vehicle transporting loose materials must have the load completely covered with a canvas or tarp tightly secured to prevent spillage onto highways.

questions.prompt: How does pulling a heavy trailer or boat affect vehicle handling and stopping distance?

options.text: Decreases stopping distance because trailer weight adds ground tire grip
Has zero impact on braking or handling provided trailer has small wheels
Significantly increases stopping distance and causes swaying at higher speeds
Allows passenger vehicles to accelerate faster onto freeway entrance ramps

questions.prompt: Under Texas Transportation Code §545.409, what is the maximum legal length of a tow bar or connection chain?

options.text: May not exceed twenty-five feet in length between the vehicles being towed
May not exceed five feet in length between the vehicles being towed
Tow chains have zero statutory length limits under Texas transportation laws
May not exceed fifteen feet in length between the vehicles being towed

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.409(a), the drawbar or other connection between a towing vehicle and towed vehicle may not exceed 15 feet in length, and must display a white flag if a chain or rope.

lesson_title: LESSON 07: Sharing the Road & Special Circumstances
topic_title: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning — Causes & Avoidance

questions.prompt: What physical sensory characteristics make carbon monoxide (CO) gas exceptionally dangerous?

It smells intensely of rotten sulfur eggs, causing instant sneezing reactions
It displays a thick neon yellow cloud that obscures vehicle windshield glass
It burns driver throat tissues instantly upon entering passenger vehicle cabins

questions.statutory_rationale: Carbon monoxide is an invisible, odorless, tasteless, and non-irritating toxic gas produced by internal combustion engines. Victims become drowsy and unconscious without realizing they are poisoned.

questions.prompt: What are the common early physical symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning in vehicle occupants?

options.text: Extreme hunger, rapid hair growth, and heightened hearing perception
Headache, dizziness, fatigue, nausea, blurred vision, and sudden drowsiness
Immediate muscle cramps in the feet and severe loss of dental sensation
Intense itching on the palms of the hands and ringing in the ear canals

questions.statutory_rationale: Early symptoms include headache, lightheadedness, nausea, sleepiness, confusion, and weakness. Continued exposure leads to unconsciousness, brain damage, and fatal asphyxiation.

questions.prompt: Why should you never warm up a vehicle engine inside an enclosed garage, even with the garage door open?

options.text: The cold concrete floor will cause passenger car tires to develop flat spots
Exhaust fumes will coat automotive spark plugs with heavy black carbon soot
CO gas accumulates rapidly to lethal concentrations and seeps into the home living space
Municipal city fire codes impose automatic hundred-dollar fines on vehicle idling

questions.statutory_rationale: Even with garage doors open, deadly carbon monoxide builds up within minutes and easily seeps into adjacent house living areas. Always back out into the open driveway first.

questions.prompt: If your vehicle is stranded in winter snow or mud, what must you verify before running engine for heat?

options.text: Turn off all interior dashboard air conditioning fans to save battery current
Verify the vehicle transmission fluid is filled to the maximum dipstick mark
Remove the vehicle engine air filter to allow extra oxygen into combustion
Ensure exhaust tailpipe is clear of snow or debris; cracked tailpipe leaks fumes inside

questions.statutory_rationale: If the tailpipe is buried or blocked by snow, mud, or water, exhaust gas backs up and penetrates directly into the passenger cabin, causing fatal poisoning in minutes.

questions.prompt: Why is driving with an open rear hatchback, tailgate, or trunk lid dangerous on highways?

options.text: Aerodynamic rear vacuum suction draws vehicle exhaust fumes directly into passenger cabin
Open tailgates cause vehicles to exceed Texas commercial vehicle length limits
The vehicle electronic stability system automatically limits speed to 25 mph
It causes high-frequency wind noise that disables vehicle cellular GPS radios

questions.statutory_rationale: Air flowing over a moving car creates a low-pressure vacuum pocket behind the vehicle. An open tailgate sucks exhaust fumes back into the passenger compartment.

lesson_title: LESSON 07: Sharing the Road & Special Circumstances
topic_title: Texas Move Over / Slow Down Act Statutes

questions.prompt: Under the Texas Move Over / Slow Down Act, what must you do if you cannot safely vacate the adjacent lane?

Slow to 20 mph below posted speed limit (or 5 mph if speed limit is under 25 mph)
Slow down by precisely two miles per hour and activate hazard blinkers
Come to a complete dead stop in the active travel lane until cleared

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.157, drivers must vacate the lane closest to stopped emergency vehicles, or slow to a speed 20 mph less than the posted speed limit (or 5 mph if limit is < 25 mph).

questions.prompt: Which stopped roadside vehicles with flashing lights are protected under the Texas Move Over Act?

Exclusively municipal public transit passenger buses picking up passengers
Police, fire, EMS, tow trucks, TxDOT vehicles, utility service trucks, and stranded cars
Commercial interstate tractor-trailers parked at designated highway rest areas

questions.statutory_rationale: The Move Over Act covers police, emergency medical, fire, tow trucks, TxDOT maintenance vehicles, utility service vehicles, and recently expanded to any stationary vehicle with hazard lights.

questions.prompt: What penalties face a Texas driver who violates TTC §545.157 and causes bodily injury to a responder?

Revocation of high school diploma by the Texas Education Agency commissioner
Mandatory civil forfeiture of personal vehicle tires to county sheriffs
Class A misdemeanor punishable by fines up to $4,000 and up to one year in county jail

questions.statutory_rationale: A standard violation carries fines up to $200 (or $500-$1,250 on second offense). However, if the violation results in bodily injury, it is a Class A misdemeanor (up to $4,000 fine / 1 yr jail).

questions.prompt: Why was the Move Over / Slow Down Act enacted into Texas statutory law?

options.text: To prevent fatal collisions where passing vehicles strike first responders on shoulders
To generate municipal parking fine revenue for rural county sheriff offices
To reduce roadway pavement wear caused by heavy emergency vehicle tire chains
To mandate that all Texas drivers complete annual roadside first aid exams

questions.statutory_rationale: Officers, paramedics, tow operators, and road workers are frequently struck and killed by inattentive drivers clipping them on highway shoulders. The law creates a mandatory safety buffer.

questions.prompt: On a four-lane highway with two lanes in your direction, what is your initial primary duty when approaching?

options.text: Accelerate rapidly past the vehicle to minimize exposure time alongside shoulder
Vacate the lane closest to the stopped emergency vehicle by moving to the left lane
Sound your vehicle horn continuously to warn emergency crew of your approach
Straddle the center dashed lane marking between both highway travel lanes

questions.statutory_rationale: If driving on a highway with two or more lanes in the same direction, your first statutory duty is to move out of the lane closest to the emergency vehicle if lane change is safe.

lesson_title: LESSON 07: Sharing the Road & Special Circumstances
topic_title: Safely Operating Near Oversize & Overweight Vehicles

questions.prompt: What does a pilot escort vehicle with amber flashing lights and 'OVERSIZE LOAD' banner indicate?

options.text: A private motorcade escorting municipal politicians across county roadways
A geological surveying team mapping subterranean oil pipelines beneath highway
An extra-wide, long, or heavy transport rig follows or leads; prepare for delays/yield
A slow-moving agricultural parade celebrating annual state harvest festivals

questions.statutory_rationale: Under TTC §545.420(h), if street racing results in the death of a person, the offense is elevated to a 2nd-degree felony, carrying 2 to 20 years in prison and up to $10,000 in fines.

questions.prompt: How does excessive speed exponentially increase the physical trauma suffered during a collision?

Impact force increases with the square of speed, overcoming vehicle safety cages
Speed causes vehicle passenger airbags to deploy with decreased explosive power
Impact force increases in direct linear proportion to vehicle fuel levels

Run down the center of the tracks in the same direction the train is traveling
Remain seated inside the car with safety seatbelts buckled for crash protection
Stand directly behind the stalled automobile to push it across the rails

One mile or more (equivalent to eighteen football fields) to stop completely
Fifty feet because steel train wheels possess extreme magnetic brake shoes
A train stops almost instantaneously once the engineer engages emergency air

Permitted exclusively for commercial agricultural harvest transport vehicles

Driving at a speed where stopping distance exceeds the headlight illumination range

Low beams illuminate 50 feet; high beams illuminate 1,000 to 1,500 feet
Low beams illuminate 500 feet; high beams illuminate 2,000 feet forward
Low beams and high beams provide identical one-hundred-foot beam ranges

Look toward the right edge of your lane or white fog line until the car passes
Close your left eye completely and steer toward the yellow center stripe
Look down at the vehicle interior speedometer cluster until darkness returns

questions.statutory_rationale: Do not look directly at oncoming lights; this causes temporary retinal blindness. Look down toward the right-hand edge of your lane or the white fog line to guide your path safely.

questions.prompt: Why is the twilight period between dusk and full darkness one of the most dangerous driving times?

options.text: Highway electronic speed limit display signs temporarily turn off for recalibration
Automotive engine oil viscosity thickens rapidly during twilight temperature shifts
Fading daylight diminishes road contrast before artificial headlights become effective
Atmospheric barometric pressure drops cause sudden vehicle brake pedal vibrations

questions.statutory_rationale: During dusk and dawn, the sky still has ambient light but shadows lengthen and road contrast drops drastically. Human eyes struggle to adapt to the transition, obscuring pedestrians and hazards.

questions.prompt: How does the fatal crash rate per mile driven at night compare to daytime driving rates in Texas?

Nighttime and daytime fatal crash rates are statistically identical in Texas
Night driving is the safest driving period because highway corridors are empty
Nighttime fatal crash rates are approximately three times higher than daytime rates

questions.statutory_rationale: Despite carrying only 25% of total traffic, nighttime driving accounts for nearly half of all fatal crashes. Reduced visibility, fatigue, intoxication, and higher speeds multiply risk by three.

Permanent driver license revocation with zero administrative court hearing rights

questions.prompt: When glancing down at a text message for five seconds at 55 mph, how far does your car travel blind?

Fifty feet, allowing ample time to notice stopped intersection traffic
Glancing down does not affect the forward travel distance of moving cars

Move the vehicle immediately to the nearest shoulder, median, or off-ramp exit
Set up a lawn chair in the traffic lane to photograph skid marks with a phone
Abandon vehicle on freeway main lanes and walk across traffic to call home

Apparent damage to property of any one person amounting to $1,000 or more
Damage amounting to precisely one hundred dollars on minor bumper scrapes

Begin dismantling damaged automotive headlights to salvage copper wires

Insurance companies dispatch free replacement rental cars to the crash scene
Notifying insurers guarantees the state will forgive all future speeding fines

Human trafficking awareness instruction to help motorists recognize and report signs
Compulsory self-defense martial arts training for teenage driver education students

Approach the victim loudly and interrogate them about their immigration status

Non-criminal civil litigation settled through private administrative mediation
